title: Discovery: Redwood & Orchid AI - Latency & Throughput
summary: Intro discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency needs, and token/sec benchmarking across hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options. Customer wants short streaming responses for chat (p95 < 250ms) and batch throughput for high-concurrency inference; discussed benchmarks, GPU types, caching, and security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: run token/sec benchmark on 8k and 32k contexts, share pricing/security docs, schedule pilot kickoff.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood. with me is Priya Shah, our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya (Orchid CTO): Maya Chen here, CTO. Raj and Lina are on from infra and ML. Sam PM here too.
[00:14] Raj (Orchid ML): hey. audio a little low on my side, sorry.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): No worries. Quick agenda: figure out your p95 latency SLOs, concurrency needs, streaming requirements, and plan a token/sec benchmark. is that right Maya?
[00:26] Maya (Orchid CTO): yes, exactly. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for latency-sensitive chat features. main asks: p95 under 250ms for interactive chat responses under typical prompt sizes, support for streaming, and sustain concurrency ~150 simultaneous users  maybe burst to 500. Also need SOC2 type II and SSO.
[00:42] Jordan: great, let's unpack. Priya, do you want to start with typical model choices and perf envelopes?
[00:47] Priya: sure. From an infra POV, latency is a function of model size, seq length, and batching. For hosted we have verified profiles: small chat models (7-13B) can hit p95 sub-200ms for single-turn streaming at short sequences (<=512 tokens) with continuous streaming enabled and optimized kernels; larger 70B models are higher. Dedicated improves predictability (reserved GPU pools) and private gives you VPC/on-prem control but adds networking variability depending on customer infra.
[01:18] Raj: when you say p95 sub-200ms is that for end-to-end generation or just first-token latency? we care about time-to-first-token and overall completion too.
[01:26] Priya: good call \u2014 our numbers separate first-token latency and tokens-per-second after that. First-token p95 is dominated by model forward pass and KV cache warmup; for a 13B-style model we often see first-token p95 ~120-180ms on A100-like GPUs in our hosted environment. Streaming throughput after first token can be 200-800 tokens/sec depending on quantization and model.
[01:46] Lina (Infra): what about concurrency implications? if we have 150 concurrent users each streaming, do you multiplex on GPUs or do we need dedicated instances per customer?
[01:54] Priya: we use a continuous-batching runtime. for hosted, requests are dynamically batched; effective latency depends on load shape and batching window. At moderate concurrency, batching helps throughput but can increase latency if you allow larger batch windows. For Dedicated you can reserve capacity to meet p95 SLOs by sizing pools \u2014 we can model expected throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU and size accordingly. Example: an 8xA100 pool can sustain X tokens/sec \u2014 we'll run empirical benchmarks tailored to your prompts.
[02:24] Maya: what's realistic tokens/sec per GPU? numbers we've seen from other vendors vary a lot \u2014 we saw claims of 2k tokens/sec per GPU for small models.
[02:33] Priya: right, claims vary. For quantized 13B variants on an A10/A100 class device, 1k\u20132k tokens/sec is typical in our tests for streaming small-token payload after warmup. For 70B the number drops to a few hundred tokens/sec. But benchmarks depend on seq lengths and whether KV caching/prefix reuse is possible.
[02:53] Raj: we'll mostly do chat with user messages ~60\u2013150 tokens and model responses 20\u201380 tokens. We also have some long context sessions up to 8k tokens for retrieval-augmented generation. How does context length affect these numbers?
[03:07] Priya: context length impacts memory and kernel selection; p95 for first-token on long contexts (8k or 32k) increases because of KV cache ops and attention overhead. We typically see first-token latency double for 8k vs 512 in some setups. However, with optimized kernels and chunked attention, we can mitigate. That's why we recommended running token/sec benchmarks at both 512 and 8k contexts.
[03:33] Jordan: can I ask about failover/fallback? if you're on Hosted and latency spikes, can requests go to a smaller model variant or to Dedicated?
[03:41] Priya: yes \u2014 smart routing can fallback to lower-latency model variants or different regions/tier. We can set automatic fallback policies by route. This avoids full outages but may change output quality.
[03:52] Sam (PM): security: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, and customer-managed KMS. also audit logs and retention controls. is that all in scope for Private or Hosted as well?
[04:02] Jordan: hosted supports SOC2, SSO, and integrations with customer KMS for key scoping on Dedicated and Private. Private (VPC/on-prem) is preferred for strict residency and in-network HSM. We'll share our security pack after the call.
[04:15] Maya: thanks. back to numbers: what would you propose for a pilot to validate p95 250ms at 150 concurrency?
[04:23] Priya: pilot plan: 1) share a short benchmark harness (script) and a sample prompt set; 2) Redwood runs an initial hosted benchmark using a model configuration you select (e.g., 13B quantized) to measure first-token p95 and sustained tokens/sec; 3) if hosted looks close, we run a Dedicated sizing simulation and an on-prem smoke test if you want Private. We'll measure both streaming latency and aggregate throughput under simulated traffic including cold/warm cache scenarios.
[04:50] Raj: about caching \u2014 do you support prefix/K V cache across sessions? if we have retrieval results we want to cache effectively.
[04:57] Priya: we have prefix caching and KV cache reuse; it helps a lot for repeated system prompts or retrieval-augmented sections. That can reduce repeated attention work and improve first-token latency on warm paths. cache hit behavior will be part of the benchmark.
[05:10] Lina: network egress \u2014 if we pick Private in our VPC, what does network path look like? we have strict egress auditing.
[05:18] Jordan: Private gives you customer-managed networking and audit logs. our Private package can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem with an optional control plane. we'll include network topology docs.
[05:27] Maya: can you share examples of p95 numbers you measured? maybe a short table.
[05:31] Priya: sure, verbally: hosted 13B quantized on A100: first-token p95 ~130\u2013180ms (512 context), streaming sustain ~1k\u20131.5k tps; 70B on A100: first-token p95 ~350\u2013600ms, sustain 200\u2013400 tps. Dedicated numbers similar but more predictable; Private depends on your HW (we've seen good perf on 8xA100 or H100 clusters).
[06:00] Raj: what's the mitigation for jitter at p95 \u2014 do you recommend dedicated warm pools?
[06:06] Priya: warm pools, pinned KV caches, and reserving concurrency slots in Dedicated all reduce tail. Also smaller max batching windows for latency-sensitive routes. We can instrument token-level tracing to find hotspots.
[06:20] Maya: any client-side tweaks? e.g., streaming chunk sizes or early flush?
[06:25] Priya: yes, sending smaller chunks and starting a flush on first token helps perceived latency. Also do client-side retry/backoff to avoid thundering herd. We'll provide SDK guidance.
[06:35] Jordan: switching to procurement \u2014 if we pilot on Hosted and then move to Dedicated, what's the cadence?
[06:40] Priya: usually pilot 2\u20134 weeks for bench and QA, then Dedicated sizing and contract (monthly commit) \u2014 we can overlap to avoid downtime.
[06:48] Sam: pricing ballpark for Dedicated?
[06:51] Jordan: we'll send a tailored pricing sheet. ballpark depends on GPU types and committed throughput. we'll share both per-token hosted pricing and Dedicated capacity pricing in the follow-up.
[06:59] Raj: one more question \u2014 metrics to validate in pilot: we want p95 first-token, p95 end-to-end, tokens/sec, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens. any others?
[07:09] Priya: add cache hit rate, median latency, GPU utilization, and memory pressure at peak. We'll instrument those in the benchmark report.
[07:17] Maya: cool. any concerns about model quality if you fall back to a smaller model for latency?
[07:23] Priya: yes \u2014 quality tradeoffs are real. we recommend a canary with A/B to measure quality delta. Redwood Optimize can recommend model/quantization tradeoffs per workload.
[07:34] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps. Priya?
[07:36] Priya: I'll own running the initial hosted benchmark with Orchid's prompt set. deliverables: 1) hosted benchmark report (first-token p95, sustain tokens/sec, p50/p95 for end-to-end) 2) Dedicated sizing recommendation 3) notes on caching and config. Need sample prompts + expected user patterns from Raj and Maya.
[07:51] Raj: we'll provide prompt set and sample traffic profile by EOD Friday (2026-03-19).
[07:57] Maya: timeline wise we want pilot results within two weeks of benchmark.
[08:02] Jordan: I'll send pricing and security docs today. Also we'll propose pilot dates.
[08:07] Lina: can you include a checklist for Private deployment network requirements?
[08:10] Jordan: yes, we'll attach network checklist and the security pack.
[08:14] Sam: any blockers on our side? maybe shared data for benchmarking \u2014 we might need non-prod dataset obfuscated for quality evals.
[08:21] Priya: we can accept obfuscated sample prompts; or Redwood can run synthetic workloads if you can't share.
[08:27] Maya: we'll try to share obfuscated. good.
[08:30] Jordan: cool. any other questions?
[08:33] Raj: minor \u2014 how do you measure p95 for streaming where tokens arrive incrementally?
[08:38] Priya: we measure time-to-first-token and time-to-completion for the full response. For p95 we report both; streaming perceptual latency is often better even if end-to-end is longer.
[08:49] Maya: perfect. thanks both.
[08:53] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and a benchmark plan.
[08:58] Meeting ends with quick goodbyes and action confirmations.

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and shorthand (e.g., "K V cache" for KV cache, "Samell" mis-heard for SAML in audio), and timestamps are approximate.

Orchid to share obfuscated prompt set and traffic profile by 2026-03-19 (Raj/Maya)

Schedule pilot kickoff pending benchmark results (Jordan & Maya)
